justifications.r1: Cheap mana rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Indulgence, Fellwar Stone) and explosive ritual mana (Skirk Prospector, Brightstone Ritual, Battle Hymn, Infernal Plunge, Springleaf Drum) deploy The Great Goblin on Turn 3.
justifications.r2: S-tier card flow: The Great Goblin exiles the top card of the library on every Goblin, Orc, or Army death playable through the end of your next turn, augmented by Skullclamp, Rundvelt Hordemaster, Goblin Ringleader, and Village Rites.
justifications.a1: A-tier selection and redundancy anchored by Goblin Matron tutoring any Goblin directly to hand, high density of token generators, and multiple free sacrifice outlets.
justifications.a2: Achieves engine readiness by Turn 4 via low-cost Goblin token curves and deploying The Great Goblin.
justifications.p1: Critical onset hits by Turn 6 as continuous aristocrat burn and swarm combat start threatening lethal life totals.
justifications.p2: A-tier win compactness: closing the game takes just 1 opponent response cycle after onset due to the Putrid Goblin + First Day of Class infinite persist loop or sudden Shared Animosity combat bursts.
justifications.p3: Goblin swarm on the battlefield, visible sacrifice outlets, and counter placement telegraph lethal lines.
justifications.i1: B-tier reactive disruption suite featuring Terminate, Bedevil, Fell the Profane, Vandalblast, Gempalm Incinerator, and Goblin Bombardment.
justifications.i2: B-tier proactive denial: repeatable board suppression via Goblin Bombardment, Pashalik Mons, Sling-Gang Lieutenant, and Goblin Chainwhirler wiping token armies.
justifications.s1: B-tier plan shielding: Goblin Chirurgeon provides sacrifice-based regeneration, and Goblin Turncoat provides protection from red.
justifications.s2: A-tier engine recovery: chaining impulse card draws off dying creatures allows immediate rebuilding from board wipes, supported by Boggart Cursecrafter.
justifications.s3: A-tier independence: the 99 functions autonomously as a high-velocity Goblin tribal swarm, combat pump, and persist combo engine without The Great Goblin.

overview: This deck is a synergistic Rakdos Goblin aristocrats build led by The Great Goblin. The strategy focuses on flooding the battlefield with cheap Goblin tokens and converting creature deaths into card flow through the commander's impulse ability. It burns opponents whenever counters are placed on Goblins, Orcs, or Armies, rewarding mechanics like amass, mentor, and blight. The deck leverages sacrifice outlets like Skirk Prospector and Goblin Bombardment alongside drain payoffs like Pashalik Mons, Bastion of Remembrance, and Boggart Cursecrafter. It can win through explosive combat steps with Shared Animosity or through infinite persist loops using Putrid Goblin, First Day of Class, and any free sacrifice outlet. While vulnerable to heavy enchantment-based stax and exile sweepers, the deck recovers quickly by chaining impulse draws off dying creatures.

core_strategy: Deploy cheap Goblin token producers and mana ramp during Turns 1 and 2.
Cast The Great Goblin on Turn 3 to prepare your card advantage and burn engine.
Drop sacrifice outlets and counter-placing cards on Turns 4 and 5 to exile cards and drain life totals.
Close the game on Turns 6 and 7 using Shared Animosity combat attacks, mass aristocrat burn, or a Putrid Goblin persist loop.

keep: Hands with two to three lands, at least one early mana ramp piece, and low-cost Goblin token generators like Dragon Fodder or Mogg War Marshal.
avoid: Hands without early red and black mana, or hands overloaded with expensive payoffs like Siege-Gang Commander and Bolg of the North without early curve plays.

key_tips: Use your sacrifice outlets in response to opposing removal to trigger The Great Goblin and bank exiled cards for your next turn.
Pair Putrid Goblin with First Day of Class and a sacrifice outlet for an infinite damage and infinite mana loop.
Remember that The Great Goblin triggers on any counter placed on a Goblin, including -1/-1 counters from blight and quest counters on creatures.

critical: Complete inability to remove resolved problem enchantments like Rest in Peace, Propaganda, or Humility.
Exile-based board sweepers such as Farewell and Sunfall that bypass both regeneration and on-death triggers.
moderate: Lack of stack interaction to disrupt opposing fast win attempts or protect key combo turns.
Reliance on the graveyard and death triggers makes replacement exile effects shut down primary card flow.
minor: Heavy colored mana requirements on cards like Goblin Chainwhirler can strain awkward mana draws.
Vulnerability to repeatable creature token sweepers.
